subject: Service availability baseline & staged credit plan — Fintegra
messages:
From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@fintegra.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline and credit questions

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week — the throughput numbers looked promising. Procurement asked me to pin down the availability and remedy mechanics before we move to contracting. Two quick asks up front:

- Can you confirm your standard monthly uptime commitment for the hosted API (percent uptime measured monthly, excluding scheduled maintenance)?
- What does the monthly service credit ladder look like (examples and caps)? We need a predictable exposure profile for our finance team.
- We also need a latency SLO for the text-generation endpoint (p50/p95) for our prod traffic profile.

We'd prefer a single SLA doc to hand to legal rather than multiple ad hoc exceptions. If you can send a starting template or a short proposal, I'll circulate to Liam (ops) and our procurement lead.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is trying to close by the end of the quarter.

Thanks,
Emma Clarke
Head of Platform Partnerships
Fintegra Analytics

---
P.S. attaching our service usage estimate in the follow-up if helpful (not attached here).

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@fintegra.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and credit questions

Hi Emma — great to hear, and glad the demo was useful.

Quick answers and a short proposal attached (SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf):

- Standard monthly uptime: 99.9% for the hosted inference API (measured per calendar month; downtime defined as inability to serve 5xx responses across all regional endpoints).
- Credit ladder (summary): 0–0.1% downtime = no credit; 0.1–1.0% = 5% of monthly invoice; 1.0–5.0% = 20% of monthly invoice; >5.0% = 50% of monthly invoice. Monthly cap = 30% of that month's invoice (we can discuss cap adjustments).
- Latency SLO (typical): text-generation p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms (for requests under 512 tokens on our US hosted fleet) — we'll provide a regional breakdown in the attachment.

Notes and exceptions:
- Scheduled maintenance windows (we give 48 hours' notice) are excluded from uptime calculations; we can look at reducing the maintenance window notice and duration for committed Dedicated capacity but that changes pricing.
- For your production profile we can consider a small SLA uplift (to 99.95%) with a 6–12 month commitment or reserved capacity.

Ben and Marissa are copied to discuss credit cap flexibility and any procurement constraints. If the attachment looks reasonable, Ben can turn this into a redline-friendly clause for legal.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Proposal_v2.pdf

From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@fintegra.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintegra.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline and credit questions

Avery — thanks for the quick proposal. A few concerns after circulation with ops and procurement:

1) 99.9% monthly uptime exposes us to ~43 minutes of downtime per month; our customer SLA requires ≤ 30 minutes downtime for the user-facing inference pipeline. Would Redwood consider 99.95% for the core inference endpoints we use in production?
2) The current cap (30% of monthly invoice) is pretty high from a procurement perspective — they'd like a predictable cap that scales with severity (e.g., lower cap for short outages). Can we structure a tiered cap or a blended cap that limits exposure on a single incident?
3) Maintenance carveouts: we can accept scheduled maintenance but need a tighter window (max 4 hours per month) or else we need scheduled maintenance to be scheduled in pre-agreed maintenance windows with a business impact review.

Also — can you provide an example of how credits would calculate on a real bill? If you could run a sample with our usage profile (we'll share numbers), that would be very helpful.

If we can get closer on the uptime baseline and maintenance rules, procurement is comfortable progressing.

Best,
Emma

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@fintegra.com>
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 05 Nov 2025 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service availability baseline & staged credit plan — Fintegra

Hi Emma — Ben here (sales lead on the account). Thanks for the clear ask — we've talked internally and propose a compromise that maps to your risk profile while keeping our operational guardrails intact. Summary below; see attached metrics snapshot (Prod_Metrics_snapshot.csv) that illustrates our observed mean time to recovery for similar customers.

Proposed compromise:
- Uptime: 99.95% for core text-generation production endpoints that Fintegra pins in the agreement (these will be listed by route in the redline). Remaining endpoints remain at 99.9%.
- Credits: a tiered monthly credit ladder with a per-incident trigger and a blended monthly cap:
  - Incident severity A (partial region-wide degradation > 20 min): credit = 10% of monthly bill for that incident, up to 20% monthly aggregate cap.
  - Incident severity B (regional blips 5–20 min): credit = 3% per incident, aggregated monthly cap contribution capped at 5%.
  - Catastrophic (global outage > 60 min): credit = 25% for that incident, combined with a monthly cap of 30%.
  - Overall monthly cap: 30% remains, but we will exempt single short-duration incidents from immediately consuming the cap (i.e., we aggregate by severity bands).
- Maintenance: Redwood will guarantee no more than 4 hours of scheduled maintenance affecting pinned endpoints per calendar month for Fintegra, provided maintenance is requested at least 14 days in advance and occurs in pre-agreed windows. Emergency maintenance (rare) will be communicated immediately and is subject to out-of-band coordination.
- Latency SLOs (committed for pinned endpoints): p50 ≤ 100ms, p95 ≤ 350ms (measured on production traffic post-onboarding). If we observe systemic regressions, we will trigger a joint investigation and corrective action.

Next steps:
1) If this sounds acceptable, we'll prepare a redline-ready clause listing pinned routes (we'll need your confirmation of which endpoints qualify).
2) Legal (cc: laura_bennett) will propose the formal text and a final cap structure that meets both parties' procurement/compliance needs.
3) We'll run a worked example with your usage numbers to show credit calculations — please send the monthly invoice estimate and observed p95 latencies.

We think this gives Fintegra the tighter availability you need for user-facing pipelines while keeping predictable economics. Happy to hop on a quick call if you'd prefer to iterate live.

Best,
Ben Carter
Principal Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Prod_Metrics_snapshot.csv

From: Emma Clarke <emma.clarke@fintegra.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fintegra.com>
Date: Thu, 06 Nov 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service availability baseline & staged credit plan — Fintegra

Thanks Ben — and thanks, Avery. That compromise is much closer to what procurement and ops need. A few items to lock before we hand to legal for a redline:

- We confirm the set of pinned endpoints: /v1/generate (production), /v1/chat (production). I will send a short list of exact route IDs by EOD Friday.
- Please include the worked example of credits vs our expected monthly invoice (we estimate $48,500/month) so procurement can see dollar exposure under each band.
- Maintenance process: we accept the 14-day notice and 4-hour cap for pinned endpoints, provided emergency maintenance has a documented business-impact review and a maximum 8-hour carveout per quarter.

If you can get a draft redline with those specifics (and the sample credit calculation) into DocuSign or shared Drive link early next week, procurement will prioritize. CCing Laura from our side to help coordinate the contract language.

Appreciate the responsiveness — moving this forward.

Best,
Emma Clarke
Head of Platform Partnerships
Fintegra Analytics
